cases.reason: In orthogonal_basis (case_a.py:9-20), when reducing cur against existing basis rows, the while loop breaks as soon as the highest set bit p of cur is not yet a pivot, without reducing lower set bits q < p of cur that already exist as pivots in basis. Thus basis is not in reduced row echelon form (higher-pivot rows retain nonzero entries in lower pivot columns). Consequently, reading off nullspace vectors directly from free-column bits of basis rows (case_a.py:22-29) violates the F2 orthogonality equations.

counterexample.expected_fact: With vectors [3 (0b011), 6 (0b110)] in F2^3, basis becomes {1: 3, 2: 6} because bit 1 is not cleared from 6. Actual output [3] spans {0, 3}, containing witness 3 which is not orthogonal to 6 (parity(3 & 6) = parity(2) = 1), whereas the true orthogonal complement is {0, 7} (span of [7]).

cases.proof_gap: Defect is established by a concrete counterexample; no proof of correctness is possible for the current code. Even if repaired to full RREF, this routine only computes an F2 linear subspace orthogonal complement and does not solve general SAT.

cases.reason: In partition (case_b.py:10-15), edges are scanned in a single pass and an edge is only added to active/adj if one of its vertices is already in active at the moment that edge is visited. If an edge reachable from seeds appears before the edge(s) connecting it to seeds, it is permanently skipped instead of computing transitive closure / fixpoint reachability.
cases.proof_gap: Defect is established by a concrete counterexample; the single-pass loop is order-dependent and fails to compute the full parity-connected closure whenever connecting edges appear later in the list.

cases.reason: Because every row has the same availability mask and each row must receive at least one hole with no two rows sharing a hole, a valid allocation exists iff K = sum(available) >= r (necessity: r disjoint nonempty subsets of available holes require at least r true entries; sufficiency: assign the r rows to r distinct available holes). The early exits handle r == 0 (True, since K >= 0) and r > len(available) (False, since K <= len(available) < r). For 1 <= r <= h, induction on prefix length t = 0..h establishes the loop invariant state[j] == (j <= K_t) for all 0 <= j <= r (base t=0: state[0]=True, state[1..r]=False; step: state[j] = old[j] or (bit and old[j-1]) shifts the threshold by +1 iff bit is True), preserving bool values under the contract that available is a list of booleans. At t=h, state[r] is (r <= K_h). Cost claim holds: early exits do 0 cell updates, and the loop performs exactly h*r cell updates (hence at most h*r nonzero updates).
cases.proof_gap: Soundness holds strictly under the documented uniform-availability contract (equivalent to counting available holes >= r) and does not extend to row-specific hole availabilities (bipartite matching), general pigeonhole encodings with heterogeneous clauses, or arbitrary CNF/SAT instances. The cost bound is in recurrence-cell updates (and depends on r <= h), not a general bit-time complexity proof or SAT solver bound.

cases.reason: orthogonal_basis does not maintain Reduced Row Echelon Form (RREF): the while-loop stops reducing cur as soon as its highest bit p is not in basis, without reducing cur against lower existing pivots q < p. Newly inserted basis[p] can therefore contain 1s in other pivot columns q < p, which invalidates the nullspace extraction loop (lines 22-29) that assumes each pivot row has no other pivot bits set.

counterexample.expected_fact: For n=3 and vectors=[3, 6] (0b011, 0b110), the true F2 orthogonal complement is {0, 7} (span of [7]), whereas actual=[3] spans {0, 3}. Witness 3 lies in span(actual) yet is not orthogonal to input vector 6 because popcount(6 & 3)=popcount(2)=1 is odd; conversely 7 is orthogonal to both 3 and 6 but is absent from span(actual).

cases.proof_gap: Refuted by concrete counterexample (n=3, vectors=[3, 6]). Even if fixed to full RREF, the routine only computes an F2 linear orthogonal complement via Gaussian elimination and has no general SAT-solving scope.

cases.reason: Under uniform availability across all r rows, choosing r pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets of T={j: available[j]} is feasible iff |T|>=r (by pigeonhole for necessity and distinct singletons for sufficiency, with r=0 vacuously True). For 1<=r<=len(available), induction on prefix length i shows the loop invariant state[j] == (j <= k_i) for 0<=j<=r (where k_i is the count of True entries in available[:i]): base state[j]==(j<=0), and state[j] = old[j] or (bit and old[j-1]) updates (j<=k_i) to (j<=k_i+1) when bit is True and preserves it when False, with no aliasing because a new list is allocated each step. Thus state[r] returns (r <= |T|) as a bool. Cost claim holds: 0 updates when r==0 or r>h, and h*r recurrence-cell evaluations for j=1..r when 1<=r<=h, so at most h*r nonzero/j>=1 recurrence-cell updates.
cases.proof_gap: Sound universally under its exact documented contract (nonnegative int r, boolean list available, identical availability for every row). Scope limit: this is a restricted symmetric feasibility check equivalent to sum(available)>=r; it does not handle row-specific availability (bipartite matching), multi-constraint formulas, or arbitrary CNFs, and makes no general SAT or Turing-machine bit-time claim. Finite checks confirm behavior for h<=6 but the universal claim rests on the inductive invariant above; input type/domain assumptions (e.g., strict booleans in available, nonnegative int r) are contract preconditions, not enforced at runtime.

review.overall_scope: Cases a and b are incorrect under their documented contracts due to concrete algorithmic bugs (incomplete RREF reduction in a; single-pass reachability omission in b). Case c is sound under its narrow symmetric-availability contract. None of the three components—even if a and b were repaired—constitutes or implies a general polynomial-time SAT solver.

cases.reason: During basis insertion, the while loop only eliminates the current highest bit p = cur.bit_length() - 1 and breaks as soon as basis.get(p) is None, leaving lower pivot bits q < p unreduced in cur. Because lines 26-28 extract nullspace coordinates assuming full reduced row-echelon form (each basis[pivot] cleared at all other pivots), unreduced lower pivot entries corrupt the free-variable back-substitution.

counterexample.expected_fact: actual spans {0, 3}, which is not orthogonal to input 6 since parity(6 & 3) = parity(2) = 1; the true F2 orthogonal complement in [0, 8) is {0, 7} (spanned by [7]), so 3 is spuriously included and 7 is missing.

cases.proof_gap: Counterexample refutes the contract at minimal dimension n=3; fixing it would still require a formal RREF invariant proof over arbitrary n >= 0 rather than finite-n checks.

cases.reason: Lines 10-15 perform a single pass over edges in input order, activating and wiring an edge only if it already intersects active at the moment it is visited. Any earlier edge whose variables become reachable from seeds only through later edges is permanently skipped, losing reachable variables and/or failing to merge components.
cases.proof_gap: Single-pass order dependence refutes the transitive-closure contract at n=3; a sound implementation would need a fixed-point or full hypergraph BFS/union-find proof of order-independence.

cases.reason: Because every row shares the exact same availability mask and needs at least one unshared available hole, a valid allocation exists iff count(True in available) >= r (vacuously True for r == 0, impossible for r > h). After processing t holes with k_t True entries, the DP maintains the exact boolean invariant state[j] == (k_t >= j) for 0 <= j <= r via state[j] = old[j] or (bit and old[j-1]), returning state[r] after at most h*r recurrence-cell updates (0 updates when r == 0 or r > h).
cases.proof_gap: Correctness relies strictly on identical availability across rows and unit-cost Python boolean operations (at most h*r cell updates, not bit-complexity for huge integers). Extending to row-specific availability requires bipartite matching/Hall conditions, and arbitrary coupled constraints remain NP-complete; this restricted counting DP implies nothing about general polynomial-time SAT, nor do finite checks (h,r <= 6) alone establish universal or asymptotic claims.
